set.st: A hermit known as "Wolf River Jack" (John Smith; the FBI later named him William Warnick Jr.) lived alone in a shack on the Wolf River about 25 mi NE of Antigo and was found dead near it on 9 Jun 1939, killed by a blow to the head. Police believed his killer had heard he hid his money in tin cans buried in the earth; "legend was that he had a fortune buried in the woods." The two robbers beat him with a bat on 30 May 1939 to make him tell where it was and took only a cheap watch; both pleaded guilty, and one drew 7-14 years in February 1940. No amount and no proof it existed. The pin marks Lily, not the shack.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: the 1939 killing is well documented, but the buried money is rumor only, no amount, and nothing was found; the shack is unplaced.
